div.p: I was born and raised in Ashoknagar, an urban town near Kolkata. From a very young age, I was deeply drawn to anything creative. Long before I knew what digital design was, I was constantly working with my hands making handmade crafts, painting, and drawing. For me, creativity wasn't just a hobby; it was my primary way of expressing myself and understanding the world around me. Those early days spent sketching and crafting from scratch laid the artistic foundation for the way I look at design today.

My academic journey was a process of continuous exploration. A pivotal shift happened back in 2015, while I was in the 10th standard, when I got my first PC. As I spent more time online, I constantly ran into frustrating user issues and clunky websites. Because I've always been someone who wants to fix things, I started looking into how I could solve these digital roadblocks myself. That curiosity led me directly to the world of UI/UX. Later, as I attended West Bengal State University (WBSU) and graduated with a degree in Arts, I realized I could perfectly combine my traditional artistic background with this new problem-solving mindset to fix the very issues I faced as a user. From there, I dove headfirst into learning the craft.

Today, I bring that same childhood creativity and "fixer" mentality into my career as a UI/UX Designer. With over five years of professional experience working remotely, I specialize in transforming complex problems into seamless, user-centric digital products. My day-to-day focus ranges from architecting large-scale, scalable design systems in Figma for robust SaaS platforms to exploring innovative ways AI can streamline workflows for digital managers.

Beyond the screen, I carry an entrepreneurial spirit and a love for adventure, often heading out on my Royal Enfield for solo trips to find fresh inspiration. Whether I am crafting a digital interface or exploring a new road, my goal is always to build meaningful, impactful experiences that connect with people.

div.h1: Wexa AI Onboarding Flow Independent UX Audit and Improvised Redesign

div.p: This is an independent concept case study created to identify usability issues and redesign the Wexa AI onboarding flow. The goal is to reduce friction, improve usability and accessibility, and create a more intuitive onboarding experience. This project is not affiliated with or commissioned by Wexa AI.

div.span: UX Audit, UX Research, UI Design

div.p: During my audit of the existing onboarding flow, I identified several usability issues that increased cognitive load, created unnecessary friction, and made the setup process feel longer than necessary. I evaluated the experience using Nielsen's Heuristics, Jakob's Law, and established UX best practices.

div.div: Problem: No Way to Go Back
div.p: The onboarding flow doesn't allow users to revisit or modify their previous answers.

div.span: Users often refine their decisions as they learn more about the product. Without a way to go back, they may feel trapped, lose confidence in their choices, or restart the onboarding entirely.

div.p: The onboarding displays the questionnaire alongside a profile preview that appears interactive.

div.span: Users expect onboarding to focus on one task at a time. The preview competes for attention and suggests interactions that aren't available, creating unnecessary cognitive load and confusion.

div.div: Problem: Conversational Layout Creates Visual Noise
div.p: Questions are presented in a chat-style interface, showing previous messages throughout the onboarding process.

div.span: While conversational layouts work well for messaging apps, onboarding benefits from a structured, step-by-step flow. Displaying previous questions adds visual clutter without helping users complete the task.

div.p: The onboarding only displays a progress bar without indicating the current step or the total number of steps.

div.span: Users are more comfortable completing tasks when they understand how much work remains. Without clear progress information, the process feels uncertain and potentially longer than it actually is.

div.div: Problem: GitHub Integration Requires Manual Setup
div.p: Users must generate a GitHub personal access token, copy it manually, and enter their username during setup.

div.span: Manual configuration increases effort and introduces opportunities for mistakes. A lengthy setup process can discourage users from completing onboarding, especially when simpler authentication methods are widely available.

div.p: The UX audit revealed that the existing onboarding experience introduced unnecessary friction, divided users' attention, and lacked a sense of control. Rather than addressing each issue individually, I established a set of design principles to guide every design decision. These principles ensured the redesigned experience remained consistent, user-centered, and aligned with established usability best practices.

div.span: Manual configuration increases effort and introduces opportunities for mistakes. A lengthy setup process can discourage users from completing onboarding, especially when simpler authentication methods are widely available.

Users should always feel in control of their journey. I introduced clear navigation, including Previous, Skip, and Edit actions, allowing users to review, modify, or skip information without feeling trapped.

The interface was simplified by removing unnecessary visual elements, improving information hierarchy, and progressively revealing content. This helps users process information more easily and complete tasks with less mental effort.

Complex setup processes create friction during onboarding. Wherever possible, manual configuration was replaced with streamlined interactions, such as OAuth authentication, to reduce effort and minimize setup errors.
Build Trust Through Review Before Confirmation

Instead of displaying an interactive-looking preview throughout the onboarding, I moved it to a dedicated review step. This gives users an opportunity to verify and edit their information before completion, increasing confidence without interrupting the question flow.

div.p: Applying the design strategy, I restructured the onboarding flow into a focused, step-by-step experience. Each design decision directly addresses a usability issue identified during the audit, creating a more intuitive and user-friendly onboarding journey.

div.div: Solution: Introduced a Focused, Step-by-Step Flow

div.span: - Redesigned the onboarding into a single-question-per-screen experience.
- Removed the side-by-side profile preview from the onboarding flow.
- Introduced a cleaner visual hierarchy with one clear primary action.
Presenting one task at a time helps users focus on the current decision without unnecessary distractions. This approach aligns with familiar onboarding patterns and reduces cognitive load.

div.div: Solution: Introduced a Focused, Step-by-Step Flow

div.span: - Added Previous and Skip actions to every onboarding step.
- Enabled users to navigate freely between steps without losing progress.
Giving users control over their journey reduces anxiety and allows them to revisit or modify previous decisions whenever needed.

div.div: Solution: Introduced a Focused, Step-by-Step Flow

div.span:
- Added a progress indicator with explicit step numbers
(e.g., Step 2 of 5).
- Kept progress visible throughout the onboarding process.
Displaying clear progress helps users understand how much of the onboarding remains, making the experience feel shorter and more predictable.

div.div: Solution: Introduced a Focused, Step-by-Step Flow

div.span: - Replaced the manual GitHub Personal Access Token setup with OAuth authentication.
- Eliminated the need to manually enter usernames and tokens.
A one-click authentication flow significantly reduces setup effort, minimizes configuration errors, and creates a smoother onboarding experience.

div.div: Solution: Introduced a Focused, Step-by-Step Flow

div.span: - Introduced a final review screen displaying all collected information.
- Added Edit actions for each section, allowing users to make changes before completing setup.
Separating the review process from the onboarding questions keeps users focused during setup while still providing an opportunity to verify and refine their information before submission.

div.p: The redesigned onboarding transforms a conversation-based, multi-focus experience into a guided, step-by-step workflow. By applying established UX principles, the new design reduces cognitive load, simplifies setup, improves user control, and creates a more confident and intuitive onboarding experience.

div.span: - Reduced cognitive load through progressive disclosure.
- Improved user confidence with better navigation and review options.
- Faster onboarding by simplifying GitHub authentication.
- Improved user confidence with better navigation and review options.
- Clearer progress visibility, reducing uncertainty and drop-off.
- A more intuitive and predictable onboarding experience aligned with users' expectations.
